Nuevo Laredo's Cabildo unanimously approved the city's proposed 2027 Revenue Law, projecting income of more than 5.169 billion pesos for fiscal year 2027, according to CML Noticias.

The approval came during the Cabildo's 70th Ordinary Session, chaired by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, after a technical and financial analysis by the Treasury and Finance Secretariat, according to the report.

The proposal sets out the resources the city expects to receive in 2027 to fund public services, programs and municipal projects, according to CML Noticias.

The projected revenue would come from taxes, fees, products, aprovechamientos, and federal and state participations and contributions, according to the report.

Municipal Treasurer Martín Reyna Carmona said the proposal raises revenue from property tax by 7 percent, fees by 7 percent, products by 5 percent and aprovechamientos by 3 percent, aligned with the estimated inflation rate, according to El Diario de Nuevo Laredo. He said the proposal creates no new taxes and does not raise fees for municipal services.

Reyna Carmona said about 60 percent of the income would go to current spending, with the rest going to public investment, including machinery and equipment purchases, and to debt service, according to El Diario de Nuevo Laredo.

With the council's approval, the proposal now goes to the State Executive and the Tamaulipas Congress, which must review it and give final approval before the Revenue Law sets the legal framework for collecting municipal revenue in 2027, according to the report.

Sources: CML Noticias; Reynosa Press; El Diario de Nuevo Laredo.
